A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same ETS paper, including complete Appendices A–E. Methods, proofs, experiments, figures and tables can be matched despite additions, reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original ETS benchmark results in Table 1, parameter and reward analyses in Section 6 and Appendix D, and a generation case study.

after.justification: v2 retains these empirical results and adds AIME24 evaluation, additional reward comparisons and synchronous-versus-asynchronous runtime measurements.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2, energy estimation, self-consistency rewards, answer caching and acceleration proposals are retained. The asynchronous pipeline examined in the new Appendix D.6 was already documented in v1 Appendix B.2; its evaluation does not introduce a new algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix D.5 adds AIME24 evaluation on Qwen3-8B, extending coverage to challenging mathematical problems with long reasoning chains. MATH500, GSM8K, GPQA Diamond and HumanEval remain covered.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same Base, Beam Search, Best-of-N, Power Sampling and GRPO/VRPO comparisons. New experiments reuse existing methods. Table 5 adds reward ablations within its existing Best-of-N, ETS and ETS-IS columns.

E3.justification: The added AIME24 experiment uses 6144-token reasoning and avg@32 evaluation, with eight-GPU timing. Table 8 introduces paired synchronous/asynchronous timing controls. These supplement the retained main evaluation protocol; the newly stated lambda value does not establish a change to existing settings.

E4.justification: Table 5 extends downstream reward ablations to logits, entropy and self-certainty, previously examined through reward distributions. Appendix D.5 tests self-consistency on difficult long-chain reasoning, and D.6 measures pipeline effects. Figure 9 is revised; existing scaling, temperature, length and generation-case analyses remain.

E5.justification: New Table 7 explicitly reports AIME24 accuracy averaged over 32 samples, introducing an averaging practice not specified for v1 benchmark accuracies. This is sampling information, not evidence of 32 independent training runs. Neither version reports empirical confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1 is unchanged. New AIME24 results report 22.40 for ETS-IS, 18.54 for ETS and 21.57 for GRPO; Tables 5 and 8 add reward accuracies and execution runtimes. Figure 9's displayed distributions change while retaining the same qualitative conclusion. Table 3 revises ETS's MATH500 latency from 11.8× to 9.85×, and Table 2 corrects the GPQA Best-of-N cost bound from 20 to 30.

T1.justification: The propositions, theorems, assumptions and proofs in the main text and Appendices A–B are retained. Changes from TV to D_TV, probability notation and mathematical typesetting do not alter the reasoning or bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: training-free sampling toward the RL-optimal distribution, convergence guarantees, importance-sampling acceleration and empirical advantages across autoregressive and diffusion models. New experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.5 explains ETS-IS's long-chain advantage through cheaper exploration of more samples. D.6 attributes unequal pipeline speedups to differing parallelism despite uniform pipeline application. The Impact Statement additionally asserts accessibility and environmental benefits; existing limitations are largely retained.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly specifies lambda = 0.1. Appendix D.6 clarifies that the asynchronous pipeline is applied uniformly and used for Table 1's TTS results. Added experiments disclose token-length, averaging and GPU-count information. Section 5.2 drops the explicit INT4/FP8 examples; code access is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including Self-Give, Sparse-RL, TableCache, MineDraft and AIME24, alongside additional agentic-RL and diffusion background references. The substantive positioning against RL post-training and previous guided-sampling methods remains unchanged. Bibliographic updates to existing works are not new research relationships.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited wording and bibliographic corrections, updates conference front matter, revises the Impact Statement and adds Appendix D.5–D.6. The main exposition and section sequence remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: v2 expands Table 5, adds Tables 7–8, updates Figure 9, enlarges implementation tables and corrects maximum-value highlighting in Table 6. The generation example is retained as Table 9 rather than Table 7. Other figures retain their content despite layout reflow.

improvement.justification: The additional reward ablations, difficult-reasoning evaluation and execution controls strengthen empirical support, while the explicit lambda value improves reproducibility. These are useful, focused gains over v1's existing method and evidence. Reporting remains imperfect: Table 8's stated ETS gain of 32.6% is about 32.1% from its displayed runtimes. The benefits nevertheless support a limited overall improvement.
